title: Control
description: A verifiable mechanism that keeps one or more Requirements true, plus the evidence it produces. A Control declares what it implements, how it is checked, how often, and where the proof lands. Controls whose verification is 'automated' point at a runnable check; controls that are only prose are declared 'manual' and carry a review cadence.

implements.description: The Requirements this control covers. This is the single writer of the requirement-to-control edge; Requirements never list their controls.

appliesTo.description: Module paths this control operates on. Empty means company-wide.

verification.description: How the control is proven to be working. A control nobody checks is a claim, not a control.

method.description: 'automated' requires a `check` pointing at something a machine runs.

surface.description: Where verification executes. Vendor-neutral by construction.

check.description: Repo-relative pointer to the runnable check (file, function, workflow, or CLI command). Required when method is 'automated'.

failureMode.description: What happens when the check fails: block the merge, page the owner, open a task, raise a finding.

evidence.description: Where the proof of operation accumulates. An auditor should be able to follow each entry without asking a human where to look.

retention.description: How long this evidence is kept, e.g. '7y'.

status.description: 'operating' asserts the control has run at least once and produced evidence.

lastVerified.description: Date the control was last confirmed to be working. Stale dates are a doctor finding, not a silent pass.

compensatingFor.description: Controls this one substitutes for when the primary mechanism is unavailable.
